references.text: The description of the altar of burnt offering to be built from acacia wood, which supplements the instruction about the earth altar in Exodus 20:24.
The Lord will choose a place where His name shall dwell, and there the Israelites shall bring their burnt offerings and peace offerings.
At the place where the Lord will cause His name to dwell, they shall bring their burnt offerings, peace offerings, tithes, and vow offerings.
Abram built an altar to the Lord who had appeared to him, an example of worshiping at the place where God reveals Himself.
The Lord appeared to Isaac and promised to bless him, and Isaac built an altar there and called upon the name of the Lord.
God commands Jacob to build an altar in Bethel, the place where God had revealed Himself to him.
Detailed instructions regarding burnt offerings from cattle, as mentioned in Exodus 20:24.
Instructions concerning peace offerings (שְׁלָמִים) from cattle, corresponding with the peace offerings mentioned in the verse.
All peace offerings shall be brought to the tent of meeting, to the dwelling place of the Lord, to be sacrificed there.
Solomon asks the people to turn toward the temple in prayer, the place where the Lord's name dwells, and God promises to hear and forgive.
The Lord appears to Solomon and confirms that He has chosen the temple as a place for His name, promising to hear prayers offered from there.
Our altar is Christ, and through Him we shall offer sacrifices of praise to God, the fruit of lips that confess His name.
Isaiah expands and specifies the promise of God's presence at the altar from Exodus to apply to global worship.
The psalm challenges and completes the instruction in Exodus by emphasizing that God's delight in sacrifice depends on righteousness, not merely ritual.
Isaiah shows how the nations fulfill the promise of coming to God's altar to be blessed.
Deuteronomy specifies the centralization of sacrifices that were permitted in multiple locations in Exodus.
The verses belong together in the same narrative about the transition from random altars to the fixed meeting tent.
Deuteronomy 27:6 modifies the requirements from Exodus 20:24 by prescribing stone altars for the new stronghold in Canaan.
Deuteronomy 12:11 specifies and centralizes the principle of God's presence at the altar that was introduced in Exodus 20:24.
